prompt.context_jp: 忍び足でシンク越しに首を伸ばしたそのとき、背後の暖簾がふわりと持ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼が最も見られたくない相手___、腕を組んで立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces a newly revealed, unexpected figure.

feedback.correct_en: The person Kō least wanted to be seen by appears suddenly — it's new information for both Kō and the reader, so が marks it as the just-noticed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame this person as an already-established topic, flattening the dramatic reveal. を doesn't fit — this clause has no transitive verb taking that person as object.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアを開けると、知らない男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: When I opened the door, an unknown man was standing there. (new info → が)

contrast_examples.jp: その男は、いつも腕を組んで立っている。
contrast_examples.en: That man always stands with his arms crossed. (established topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「ママは知ってるんですよね？ どんな人か」
prompt.prompt_jp: 知らないわよ オーナーだけね 知ってるの___
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft-style answer identifying who knows.

feedback.correct_en: 「知ってるのは」sets up a topic ("as for the one who knows…") and the answer「オーナーだけ」has already been given — は fits this inverted cleft used for emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be used if 知ってるの were presented as new info; here the identification has already been fronted. を doesn't match the structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 知っているのは私だけです。
contrast_examples.en: The only one who knows is me. (topic-comment cleft → は)

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が知っているの？
contrast_examples.en: Who knows? (asking for new info → が)

prompt.context_jp: 店の賑わいの届かないマンションの一室で、ハナはひとり、自作の試作品をそっと口に運んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰にも見られない場所でしか、彼女___チョコレートに触れることを自分に許せなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: this sentence continues to talk about Hana as the established topic.

feedback.correct_en: Hana is the ongoing topic across the paragraph; は continues framing the whole statement about her inner rule.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 彼女 as newly identified, but she has just been named. を doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は人前では何もできない。
contrast_examples.en: She can't do anything in front of others. (ongoing topic → は)

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき彼女が立ち上がった。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment she stood up. (new event focus → が)

prompt.context_jp: スクリーンには自ら描いた新ブランドの試作案が映し出されていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会長である祖父の俊太郎の顔___、正面の最も遠い席から静かに彼を見返していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the grandfather's face being newly brought into focus.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator pans the camera to the grandfather's face as a fresh presence in the scene — a presentational use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the face was already an active topic; it's just being introduced. で doesn't match — this is the subject that stares back.

contrast_examples.jp: 廊下の奥から祖父の声が聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: Grandfather's voice came from down the hall. (new presence → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 祖父は無言だった。
contrast_examples.en: Grandfather was silent. (topic already in play → は)

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮のプレゼンが終わった直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会長___最後まで表情を変えずに聞いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the chairman is already the focus of the paragraph.

feedback.correct_en: The chairman has been the thematic anchor of the scene. は carries that topic forward and comments on his demeanor.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would highlight him as a newly introduced actor, which clashes with the ongoing scene. も would mean 'the chairman too,' implying others — not supported.

contrast_examples.jp: 会長は何も言わなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The chairman said nothing. (established topic → は)

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき会長が立ち上がった。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment the chairman stood up. (sudden event → が)

prompt.context_jp: 健二がハナの家で鍋を火にかける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 湯気の匂いを吸い込むハナの表情だけ___、この場での彼の報酬だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「だけ」 identifying what counts as his reward.

feedback.correct_en: 「〜だけが」marks an exhaustive identification: 'that and nothing else' is his reward — classic exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「だけは」would mean 'at least that one thing (in contrast to others),' which doesn't match the sense of unique sufficiency here. を doesn't fit the copular predicate.

contrast_examples.jp: 君の笑顔だけが欲しい。
contrast_examples.en: Your smile is the only thing I want. (exhaustive → が)

contrast_examples.jp: それだけはやめて。
contrast_examples.en: Just that one thing — stop. (contrastive carve-out → は)

prompt.context_jp: 大会の日の回想。
prompt.prompt_jp: 審査員たちの中でただひとり、彼女の椅子のそばに歩み寄ってきたの___、まだ現役だった健二だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft that identifies exactly which judge approached.

feedback.correct_en: This is an exhaustive-listing cleft: 'the one (and only one) who walked over was Kenji.' が picks out that unique person.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be used if the cleft phrase were an already-known topic; here the whole point is to identify who it was. で doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に話したのが彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who spoke first was him. (exhaustive id → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が話したのは昨日だ。
contrast_examples.en: It was yesterday that he spoke. (topic cleft → は)

prompt.context_jp: 健二と元美がクリニックで話す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話題___自然と、まだ若い患者の頑なな心のほうへと寄っていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 話題 as the ongoing subject of comment.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator frames 'the conversation' as a topic and comments on its drift. は is natural for this reflective summary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 話題 as a brand-new element popping into the scene, which doesn't fit a quiet narrative transition. に marks location/direction, not subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 話題は自然に恋愛に移った。
contrast_examples.en: The topic naturally drifted to love. (narrative topic → は)

contrast_examples.jp: 急に新しい話題が出た。
contrast_examples.en: A new topic suddenly came up. (new introduction → が)

prompt.context_jp: 集団カウンセリングの場で。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壮亮の理屈っぽい説明___場の空気を冷やしかけたとき、輪の反対側で、ひとりの男性が突然肩を震わせ始めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the subordinate 「〜とき」 clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside subordinate clauses like 「〜とき」, subjects normally take が, not は. The explanation is also a new element driving the next event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は tends to scope over the whole main clause and sounds odd inside a 「とき」 clause. を is wrong — 説明 is the subject here, not the object.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が話し始めたとき、電話が鳴った。
contrast_examples.en: When he began to speak, the phone rang. (subordinate subject → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は話し始めた。
contrast_examples.en: He began to speak. (main-clause topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮がカウンセリング室に残され…
prompt.prompt_jp: 従兄の姿___すでに部屋から消えており、代わりに置かれた小さな包みを、彼は落ち着かなげに膝の上で回していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle contrasting the vanished cousin with the gift that remains.

feedback.correct_en: は draws a contrast: as for the cousin, he's gone; what's there instead is the package. The 「代わりに」 structure signals this contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 従兄の姿 as new information, but the cousin is already in play from earlier. も ('also') contradicts the contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄はもう帰ったが、手紙は残っていた。
contrast_examples.en: My brother had already left, but the letter remained. (contrast → は)

contrast_examples.jp: そこに兄が現れた。
contrast_examples.en: There my brother appeared. (new arrival → が)

prompt.context_jp: レストランで知らない番号から電話が…
prompt.prompt_jp: 予期しない相手からの電話に、ハナの心臓___一気に跳ね上がった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for her heart's sudden reaction.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden involuntary bodily event takes が — her heart leapt up as a fresh event in the narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn this into a generic statement about her heart; the moment calls for a one-time, dramatic event. で doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 心臓がドキッとした。
contrast_examples.en: My heart skipped. (sudden event → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の心臓は丈夫だ。
contrast_examples.en: Her heart is strong. (general property → は)

prompt.context_jp: ハナが椅子を立った瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 立ち上がった拍子に椅子が音を立て、給仕たちの視線___一斉に彼女に集まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the waitstaff's gazes converging on her.

feedback.correct_en: The gazes are a new element entering the scene as a single event — が marks that abrupt arrival of focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 視線 as an established topic needing comment, but it's the sudden movement that matters. を doesn't match this intransitive gathering.

contrast_examples.jp: 全員の目が彼女に向いた。
contrast_examples.en: Everyone's eyes turned to her. (event → が)

contrast_examples.jp: みんなの視線は冷たかった。
contrast_examples.en: Everyone's gazes were cold. (describing a known topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: ケーキを見つけて喜んだ直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 嬉しさに顔を上げたハナの視界___、次の瞬間、凍りついた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the sudden change in her field of vision.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden, involuntary change — 'her vision froze' — is a one-time event. が puts the camera on that moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read as a generic trait of her vision, not the shock of this instant. に is a location/target marker, not a subject marker.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の目が止まった。
contrast_examples.en: Her eyes stopped. (sudden event → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の目はいつも優しい。
contrast_examples.en: Her eyes are always kind. (general property → は)

prompt.context_jp: 会長の反応を描写する地の文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 安さと質を両立させるという理想を、彼___ただの矛盾としてはねつけようとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 彼 — the paragraph has been following the chairman.

feedback.correct_en: The chairman is the running topic of this passage; は carries the thread as the narrator comments on his stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 彼 as fresh information, but he's been center stage. も would mean 'he too,' implying another unspecified rejecter — not supported.

contrast_examples.jp: その理想を、彼は信じていなかった。
contrast_examples.en: He didn't believe in that ideal. (continuing topic → は)

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき彼が反論した。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment he objected. (sudden event → が)

prompt.context_jp: 健二が切り出す前の静かな瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼が言い出そうとしていること___、ハナは何となく察していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Hana sensed.

feedback.correct_en: 「察する」takes a direct object, and the fronted phrase「〜こと」is what she senses — so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it the subject of 察する, which the verb doesn't license. に would mark a target rather than content.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の気持ちを察した。
contrast_examples.en: I sensed his feelings. (direct object → を)

contrast_examples.jp: 何かが起こる気がした。
contrast_examples.en: I had a feeling something would happen. (気がする → が)

prompt.context_jp: 会長への返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: はい まっとうな方法で ___されていないカカオを 扱うことはできません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with カカオ in this ethical context.

feedback.correct_en: 「生産される」('be produced/farmed') is the standard verb for agricultural products like cacao.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「生成」is used for chemicals or data forming; 「発生」means to occur or arise (events, phenomena) — neither fits for growing cocoa.

contrast_examples.jp: この地域で生産されるコーヒー。
contrast_examples.en: Coffee produced in this region.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題が発生した。
contrast_examples.en: A problem occurred.

prompt.context_jp: 常連客に向けての一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつも ___ ありがとうございます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the humble verb used to thank a customer for coming.

feedback.correct_en: 「いらっしゃる」is the respectful verb for the customer's coming; 「いらしていただく」thanks them for honoring us with their visit.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「行く」points away from the speaker — wrong direction. 「参る」is humble form for one's own going, not the customer's.

contrast_examples.jp: 本日はお越しいただきありがとうございます。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for coming today. (customer-raising)

contrast_examples.jp: 明日、私が参ります。
contrast_examples.en: I'll come tomorrow. (humble for one's own action)

prompt.context_jp: 健二がペアリングを語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 違うからこそ ___ がいいんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun for food-and-drink 'compatibility' / pairing.

feedback.correct_en: 「相性がいい」('to be a good match') is the fixed phrase for food pairings, personalities, etc.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「相手がいい」isn't a set phrase in this sense. 「愛情がいい」doesn't exist as a collocation.

contrast_examples.jp: ワインとチーズは相性がいい。
contrast_examples.en: Wine and cheese go well together.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼とは相性が悪い。
contrast_examples.en: He and I don't click.

prompt.context_jp: 元美が診断を伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 日常生活や対人関係に ___ が出ている場合…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that collocates with 「出る」 to mean 'have an impact'.

feedback.correct_en: 「影響が出る」('an effect appears/shows') is a standard collocation for symptoms affecting life.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「印象が出る」isn't idiomatic in this medical sense. 「原因が出る」doesn't fit — a cause isn't something that 'appears' on daily life.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事に影響が出る。
contrast_examples.en: It affects work.

contrast_examples.jp: 原因が分からない。
contrast_examples.en: The cause is unknown.

prompt.context_jp: 健二が壮亮を励ます場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 目が ___ なくたって 恋はできるんだから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes '(can't) make eye contact'.

feedback.correct_en: 「目を合わせる」('to meet eyes') is the set phrase; its potential-negative is 「目を合わせられない」.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「目を見られる」would mean 'be seen in the eye' and misses the mutual-gaze nuance here. 「目を開ける」just means to open one's eyes.

contrast_examples.jp: 恥ずかしくて目を合わせられない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm too embarrassed to meet their eyes.

contrast_examples.jp: 目を見て話しなさい。
contrast_examples.en: Look me in the eye when you talk.

prompt.context_jp: ママの朝礼。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気持ちを ___ のに 我々のチョコレートが お役に立つ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for conveying one's feelings.

feedback.correct_en: 「気持ちを伝える」is the standard collocation for conveying heartfelt feelings — exactly the Valentine's framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「気持ちを教える」sounds like teaching facts about one's feelings. 「気持ちを話す」is 'talk about feelings' and is less idiomatic for the romantic giving-of-chocolate frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 感謝の気持ちを伝えたい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to convey my gratitude.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に本当のことを話した。
contrast_examples.en: I told him the truth.

prompt.context_jp: 剣道君の話を振られて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私は ___ のが好きなんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'watching/admiring from afar'.

feedback.correct_en: 「眺める」carries the nuance of gazing at length, often from a distance — fitting Hana's quiet admiration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「探す」means to search for. 「覗く」('peek') has a sneakier, voyeuristic feel that clashes with the sentimental tone here.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠くから景色を眺める。
contrast_examples.en: Gaze at the scenery from afar.

contrast_examples.jp: 鍵穴から覗く。
contrast_examples.en: Peek through the keyhole.

prompt.context_jp: 会長の反論。
prompt.prompt_jp: 我が社の商品は 誰でも手に入る安さが 最大の ___ であり 誇りなんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun paired with 「誇り」 to describe the company's strongest selling point.

feedback.correct_en: 「魅力」('appeal, charm') pairs naturally with 「誇り」 ('pride') in a boast about a product's strength.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「問題」('problem') would reverse the meaning. 「特徴」('feature') is too neutral and doesn't fit the emphatic 「最大の〜であり誇り」 pairing.

contrast_examples.jp: 価格が最大の魅力です。
contrast_examples.en: The price is the biggest draw.

contrast_examples.jp: それが最大の問題だ。
contrast_examples.en: That's the biggest problem.

prompt.context_jp: 店で客が店員にすすめを尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: A customer asking the clerk for a recommendation. Which sounds most natural?

feedback.correct_en: 「お薦めありますか？」with the honorific お- is the natural way customers ask for a shop's recommendation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「推薦」is used for recommending a person (e.g., a candidate), not products. 「います」is for animate beings — a recommendation isn't animate.

contrast_examples.jp: 何かお薦めはありますか？
contrast_examples.en: Do you have any recommendations?

contrast_examples.jp: 彼を推薦します。
contrast_examples.en: I recommend him (as a person).

prompt.context_jp: 店員が商品を取りに行くとき。
prompt.prompt_en: A shop clerk saying 'I'll bring it right away.' Which is most natural in service register?

choices.text: すぐお持ちいたしますね。
すぐ持ってあげますね。

feedback.correct_en: 「お持ちいたします」is the humble form expected from staff addressing a customer — polite and self-lowering.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「持ってあげます」('I'll bring it for you') sounds condescending from a clerk. 「持ちますね」is plain and too casual for a shop.

contrast_examples.jp: お荷物、お持ちいたします。
contrast_examples.en: I'll carry your bag. (humble service register)

contrast_examples.jp: それ、持ってあげるよ。
contrast_examples.en: I'll carry that for you. (friendly, casual)

prompt.context_jp: 健二がハナに優しく尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: An older mentor gently asking a young woman if she's ever lonely. Which sounds most natural?

choices.text: 寂しい時もありますか？
寂しい時もあるんだぜ？

feedback.correct_en: 「〜だろ？」is a warm, familiar sentence-final used by an older male friend/mentor — fits Kenji's tone with Hana.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite 「ありますか」 breaks the intimate register they share. 「〜んだぜ」 is boastful/masculine-swaggery and would feel pushy here.

contrast_examples.jp: 疲れただろ？
contrast_examples.en: You're tired, aren't you? (warm, familiar)

contrast_examples.jp: お疲れになりましたか？
contrast_examples.en: Are you tired? (polite distance)

prompt.context_jp: 健二がハナを誘う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Reassuring Hana that the restaurant will be privately booked. Which is most natural?

choices.text: 貸し切りだよ ぜ～んぶ
貸し出しだよ ぜ～んぶ
借り切るだよ ぜ～んぶ

feedback.correct_en: 「貸し切り」is the fixed noun for a private/exclusive booking of a venue — the right word here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「貸し出し」means lending (books, tools). 「借り切る」is a verb and doesn't take 「だよ」 directly like this; also the perspective (borrowing vs. being-privately-held) is off.

contrast_examples.jp: 今夜は貸し切りです。
contrast_examples.en: Tonight is a private booking.

contrast_examples.jp: 本の貸し出しは2週間です。
contrast_examples.en: Book loans are for two weeks.
